title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Chemical Equilibrium — 2024
subject: chemistry
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State Le Chatelier's principle. Predict the effect of increasing pressure on: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)
questions.solution:
**Le Chatelier's principle:** If a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to counteract the change.

Increasing pressure favors the side with fewer moles of gas.
Reactants: 1+3 = 4 moles; Products: 2 moles.
Equilibrium shifts **towards NH₃ (right)** — Haber's process uses high pressure for this reason.
questions.knowledgeNote: If Δn = 0, pressure change has no effect on equilibrium position.

questions.question: For the reaction $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g)$, $K_c = 0.5$ at a certain temperature. If $[N_2] = 1.0$ M and $[H_2] = 0.5$ M at equilibrium, calculate the equilibrium concentration of ammonia.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Write the equilibrium constant expression**

The coefficient 3 on $H_2$ becomes a cube and the coefficient 2 on $NH_3$ becomes a square:

$$K_c = \frac{[\text{NH}_3]^2}{[\text{N}_2][\text{H}_2]^3}$$

**Step 2 — Substitute the values**

$$0.5 = \frac{[\text{NH}_3]^2}{1.0 \times (0.5)^3}$$

$$[\text{NH}_3]^2 = 0.5 \times 1.0 \times 0.125 = 0.0625$$

**Step 3 — Take the square root**

$$[\text{NH}_3] = \sqrt{0.0625} = 0.25 \ \text{M}$$

Hence the equilibrium concentration of ammonia is **0.25 M**. Notice that the very small value of $K_c$ is consistent with ammonia being formed only slowly at that temperature.
questions.knowledgeNote: Stoichiometric coefficients become powers in the equilibrium constant: $K_c = [NH₃]^2/([N₂][H₂]^3)$.
